title: Leviticus Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 25.

questions.question: Who spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai in Leviticus 25?
options: The LORD
Aaron
Joshua
Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:1 states that the LORD spoke unto Moses in mount Sinai.

questions.question: What shall the land keep when the children of Israel come into the land given to them?
options: A sabbath unto the LORD
A festival of lights
A day of fasting
A feast of harvest
questions.correctAnswer: A sabbath unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:2 commands the land to keep a sabbath unto the LORD when the children of Israel enter it.

questions.question: For how many years shall you sow your field and prune your vineyard before the sabbath year?
options: Six years
Seven years
Five years
Ten years
questions.correctAnswer: Six years
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:3 explains that six years you shall sow your field and prune your vineyard.

questions.question: What are you not allowed to do in the seventh year according to Leviticus 25?
options: Sow thy field nor prune thy vineyard
Celebrate any feast
Build houses
Harvest all crops
questions.correctAnswer: Sow thy field nor prune thy vineyard
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:4 states that in the seventh year, a sabbath of rest for the land, you shall neither sow nor prune.

questions.question: True or False: During the sabbath year, you must reap and gather all the harvest as usual.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:5 says you shall not reap or gather the grapes of the vine during the sabbath year, as it is a year of rest to the land.

questions.question: Who may eat the increase of the sabbath of the land?
options: You, your servants, strangers, and cattle
Only the priests
Only the children of Israel
No one may eat it
questions.correctAnswer: You, your servants, strangers, and cattle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:6-7 indicates that the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you, your servants, strangers, and cattle.

questions.question: How many years make up the seven sabbaths of years?
options: Forty and nine years
Fifty years
Forty years
Seventy years
questions.correctAnswer: Forty and nine years
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:8 instructs to number seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, totaling forty and nine years.

questions.question: On what day and month shall the trumpet of the jubile be sounded?
options: Tenth day of the seventh month
First day of the first month
Fifteenth day of the fifth month
Twentieth day of the ninth month
questions.correctAnswer: Tenth day of the seventh month
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:9 states the trumpet of the jubile shall be sounded on the tenth day of the seventh month.

questions.question: True or False: The fiftieth year is called a jubile where liberty is proclaimed throughout all the land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 declares the fiftieth year a jubile, proclaiming liberty throughout the land.

questions.question: What must happen for every man in the jubile year?
options: Return to his possession and family
Build a new house
Offer a sacrifice
Plant a vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Return to his possession and family
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 and 25:13 command every man to return unto his possession and family in the jubile year.

questions.question: True or False: In the jubile year, you are allowed to sow and reap as usual.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:11 forbids sowing or reaping in the jubile year; it is a holy year of rest.

questions.question: When buying or selling to your neighbour, how should the price be determined?
options: According to the number of years after the jubile
At a fixed price regardless of years
Based on the buyer's desire
The seller sets any price
questions.correctAnswer: According to the number of years after the jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:15 explains the price must be according to the years left until the next jubile.

questions.question: What is the reason given for not oppressing one another in buying and selling?
options: Because you shall fear your God
Because it is profitable
To avoid taxes
Because of the king's law
questions.correctAnswer: Because you shall fear your God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:17 says not to oppress one another but to fear your God, the LORD your God.

questions.question: What will happen if you keep God's statutes and judgments according to this chapter?
options: You shall dwell in the land in safety
You will be wealthy beyond measure
You will never face hardship
You shall become a priest
questions.correctAnswer: You shall dwell in the land in safety
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:18 promises dwelling in the land in safety if statutes and judgments are kept.

questions.question: True or False: The land will yield fruit and you shall eat your fill when you keep God's commandments.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:19 states the land shall yield fruit and you shall eat your fill.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What promise does God make to the Israelites concerning the sixth year if they obey the command to let the land rest in the seventh year?
options: He will command a blessing upon them and the land will produce fruit for three years
They will receive double harvests every year
Their enemies will be defeated automatically
They will not need to work at all
questions.correctAnswer: He will command a blessing upon them and the land will produce fruit for three years
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:20-22 explains that if the Israelites refrain from sowing and gathering in the seventh year, God will bless the sixth year to yield enough fruit for three years, showing His provision when they obey His statutes.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25, why shall the land not be sold forever?
options: Because the land is God's and the people are His sojourners
Because the land is cursed
Because the land is not valuable
Because the land is owned by the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Because the land is God's and the people are His sojourners
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:23 states the land belongs to the LORD and the Israelites are strangers and sojourners, emphasizing God's sovereign ownership over all land and people's temporary stewardship.

questions.question: What must happen if a brother becomes poor and sells some of his possession according to Leviticus 25?
options: One of his kin should redeem that which was sold
He should never return to his possession
The land is lost forever
The priest will take possession
questions.correctAnswer: One of his kin should redeem that which was sold
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:25 instructs that if a brother becomes poor and sells his possession, a relative should redeem it to restore the brother's inheritance, highlighting community responsibility and mercy.

questions.question: If the poor man has no kin to redeem his sold possession but can redeem it himself, what is he instructed to do?
options: Count the years since the sale and pay back the overplus to the buyer
Wait until the year of jubile to get it back
Give up ownership permanently
Ask the priest to redeem it
questions.correctAnswer: Count the years since the sale and pay back the overplus to the buyer
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:26-27 explains that if the man can redeem his land but has no kinsman to do so, he must calculate the time passed and pay the difference to the buyer to regain possession, reflecting fairness and justice.

questions.question: What happens to land sold if it is not redeemed before the year of jubile?
options: It remains with the buyer until the jubile year, then returns to the original owner
It becomes the permanent possession of the buyer
It is given to the priests
It becomes unproductive land
questions.correctAnswer: It remains with the buyer until the jubile year, then returns to the original owner
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:28 clarifies that sold land not redeemed stays with the buyer until the jubile, after which it reverts to the original owner, demonstrating God's provision for restoration.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25, within what time frame may a person redeem a house sold in a walled city?
options: Within a full year after it is sold
Within seven years
Only at the year of jubile
Within six months
questions.correctAnswer: Within a full year after it is sold
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:29 specifies that a sold house in a walled city can be redeemed within one full year, showing a limited period for redemption distinct from other property.

questions.question: What happens if the house in the walled city is not redeemed within the full year?
options: It becomes the permanent possession of the buyer and does not go out in the jubile
It returns to the original owner anyway
It will be sold to the Levites
It is given to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes the permanent possession of the buyer and does not go out in the jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:30 states that if the house is not redeemed within one full year, it belongs permanently to the buyer and will not revert in the jubile year, indicating a special status for houses in walled cities.

questions.question: How are houses in villages without walls treated according to Leviticus 25?
options: Like fields of the country; they may be redeemed and revert in the jubile
They become permanent possessions immediately
They belong to the Levites permanently
They cannot be sold at all
questions.correctAnswer: Like fields of the country; they may be redeemed and revert in the jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:31 explains that village houses without walls are treated as fields and may be redeemed, reverting to the owner in the jubile, emphasizing restoration and temporary ownership.

questions.question: What special privilege do the Levites have concerning the redemption of their cities and houses?
options: They may redeem their cities and houses at any time
They cannot redeem any property
Their houses are sold permanently
They must wait for the jubile to redeem
questions.correctAnswer: They may redeem their cities and houses at any time
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:32 gives the Levites the right to redeem their cities and houses whenever they choose, highlighting their unique status and perpetual possession.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 25 instruct the Israelites to treat a poor brother who has fallen into decay?
options: They must relieve him so he may live with them, even if he is a stranger or sojourner
They should ignore him and let him fend for himself
They should sell his possessions immediately
They should make him a bondservant
questions.correctAnswer: They must relieve him so he may live with them, even if he is a stranger or sojourner
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:35 teaches compassion and generosity, instructing Israelites to help their poor brothers, including strangers, to ensure they live and are supported in the community.

questions.question: What is forbidden when lending money or food to a poor brother according to Leviticus 25?
options: Charging interest or increase
Lending only small amounts
Lending to strangers only
Asking for repayment immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Charging interest or increase
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:36-37 forbids charging usury or increase when lending to a poor brother, emphasizing fairness, mercy, and reverence for God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 25, a brother sold to you because of poverty must serve as a bondservant forever without hope of release.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:39-41 clarifies that a brother sold due to poverty should serve as a hired servant until the year of jubile and then be released with his family, showing temporary servitude and God's provision for freedom.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites are instructed not to rule over their brethren with rigor but to fear God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:43 and 46 instruct the Israelites to not rule harshly over their fellow Israelites but to respect and fear God, promoting humility and kindness within the community.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 25, bondmen and bondmaids may only be taken from among the children of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:44-45 states that bondmen and bondmaids may be taken from the heathen and strangers dwelling around Israel, not from the children of Israel, who are to be treated differently.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 25 teach us about integrity when buying or selling land among neighbors?
options: Buy and sell according to the number of years left until the jubile, increasing or decreasing the price accordingly
Always sell at a fixed price regardless of years
Never sell land to neighbors
Sell land only to strangers
questions.correctAnswer: Buy and sell according to the number of years left until the jubile, increasing or decreasing the price accordingly
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:14-16 emphasizes fair pricing based on remaining years until jubile, encouraging honesty and respect among neighbors in transactions.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 25.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25, how long shall a hired servant from among your brethren serve you?
options: Until the year of jubile
For life
For seven years
Until the death of the master
questions.correctAnswer: Until the year of jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:40 states that a brother sold as a servant shall serve until the year of jubile, after which he and his children shall return to their family and possession.

questions.question: What is commanded regarding ruling over your brethren in Leviticus 25?
options: You shall not rule over him with rigour
You shall rule with strictness
You may rule as you see fit
You shall enslave your brethren
questions.correctAnswer: You shall not rule over him with rigour
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:43 commands not to rule over your brother with rigour but to fear God, emphasizing mercy among brethren.

questions.question: Who are you permitted to buy as bondmen and bondmaids according to Leviticus 25?
options: Heathen round about you
Your brethren
Levitical priests
Strangers from distant lands
questions.correctAnswer: Heathen round about you
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:44 specifies that bondmen and bondmaids should be taken from the heathen around you, not from the brethren of Israel.

questions.question: What happens if a sojourner or stranger waxes rich and your brother waxes poor and sells himself to the stranger?
options: He may be redeemed by a kinsman or himself
He will be a bondservant forever
He must leave the land
He loses all rights permanently
questions.correctAnswer: He may be redeemed by a kinsman or himself
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:48-49 allows that after being sold, the poor brother may be redeemed by a relative or by himself if able.

questions.question: How is the price of redemption determined for one sold to a stranger according to Leviticus 25?
options: According to the number of years until the year of jubile
A fixed price set by elders
Double the original sale price
Market price at the time of redemption
questions.correctAnswer: According to the number of years until the year of jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:50-52 explains the price is calculated by the years remaining until jubile, like the time of a hired servant.

questions.question: What is the status of the children of Israel in relation to God as expressed in Leviticus 25?
options: They are servants whom God brought out of Egypt
They are slaves to other nations
They are gods themselves
They have no special status
questions.correctAnswer: They are servants whom God brought out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:42 and 25:55 emphasize that the children of Israel are God's servants whom He delivered from Egypt.

questions.question: What is the significance of the year of jubile as described in Leviticus 25?
options: Liberty is proclaimed and possessions returned
All debts are doubled
Slaves are sold permanently
Land is permanently sold
questions.correctAnswer: Liberty is proclaimed and possessions returned
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10 states that the year of jubile is a time to proclaim liberty and return each man to his possession and family.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 25, houses in walled cities that are sold may be redeemed at any time and will revert at jubile.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:29-30 clarify that houses in walled cities may be redeemed only within a year; if not redeemed, they belong permanently to the buyer and do not revert at jubile.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Leviticus 25:8-10 to explain the counting of years and the jubile?
options: Chiasmus
Parable
Allegory
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:8-10 uses chiasmus, a literary structure repeating ideas in reverse order to emphasize the counting of seven sabbaths of years and the jubile, highlighting the cyclical nature of time.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares the theme of redemption and return of possession similar to Leviticus 25?
options: Jeremiah 34:8-22
Genesis 1
Exodus 20
Psalm 23
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 34:8-22
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:8-22 echoes the theme of releasing servants and returning possessions as commanded in Leviticus 25's jubile laws, emphasizing covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the concept of the year of jubile in Leviticus 25 prefigure the New Testament teaching on freedom in Christ?
options: It symbolizes liberation and restoration, fulfilled in Christ's redemption
It demands strict legalism without grace
It focuses only on agricultural laws
It abolishes all servitude permanently
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes liberation and restoration, fulfilled in Christ's redemption
questions.explanation: The jubile's proclamation of liberty (Leviticus 25:10) foreshadows spiritual freedom in Christ, as described in Galatians 5:1, where Christ sets believers free from bondage.

questions.question: What Hebrew root word underlies the term 'jubile' and what is its primary meaning?
options: Yobel, meaning ram's horn or trumpet blast
Shabbat, meaning rest
Torah, meaning law
Kadosh, meaning holy
questions.correctAnswer: Yobel, meaning ram's horn or trumpet blast
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Yobel' (יובל) literally means a ram's horn or trumpet blast, which is used to announce the year of jubile (Leviticus 25:9).

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25, what should a poor brother who sells his land do when he is able to redeem it?
options: Count the years since sale and restore the overplus to the buyer
Never attempt to redeem it
Buy land elsewhere
Sell more land to pay debts
questions.correctAnswer: Count the years since sale and restore the overplus to the buyer
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:27 commands that if a man can redeem his land, he must calculate the years since the sale and repay the excess to the buyer to regain possession.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 25:36-37 prohibit when lending to a poor brother?
options: Charging usury or interest
Lending money at all
Lending only food
Giving gifts
questions.correctAnswer: Charging usury or interest
questions.explanation: These verses forbid taking any interest or increase when lending money or food to a poor brother, emphasizing compassion and fearing God.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 25 permits perpetual sale of land without redemption.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:23 clearly states that the land shall not be sold forever because the land belongs to God, and there must be redemption provisions.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the land keeping a sabbath year as commanded in Leviticus 25:2-4?
options: It teaches God's provision and rest for creation, reflecting His holiness and care for the land.
It enforces a strict legalistic rule without spiritual meaning.
It symbolizes human mastery over nature by controlling agricultural cycles.
It requires complete idleness from all inhabitants as a form of punishment.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God's provision and rest for creation, reflecting His holiness and care for the land.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:2-4 commands the land to observe a sabbath rest every seventh year, demonstrating God's attribute of holiness and providential care for creation, ensuring both physical rest and spiritual renewal. This reflects God's sovereign provision, not just legalism or punishment.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25:6-7, what is the inclusive purpose of the sabbath of the land?
options: To provide food for all people and animals living on the land.
To punish the people for neglecting the land.
To increase the wealth of the landowners only.
To prohibit any use of the land by anyone.
questions.correctAnswer: To provide food for all people and animals living on the land.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:6-7 explains that the sabbath year produces food for the landowner, servants, strangers, and animals alike, showing God's care for all creation and His provision for social justice and ecological balance.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's sovereignty over the land is taught in Leviticus 25:23?
options: The land ultimately belongs to God, and the Israelites are merely sojourners and tenants.
The land is permanently owned by each individual Israelite.
The land can be sold forever without any divine restriction.
God has no claim on the land once it is given to the people.
questions.correctAnswer: The land ultimately belongs to God, and the Israelites are merely sojourners and tenants.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:23 declares that the land is God's possession and the Israelites are strangers and sojourners, emphasizing God's ultimate sovereignty and ownership over creation, grounding stewardship and covenantal responsibility.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 25:10-13 reveal the redemptive restoration motif within Israel's social and economic life?
options: It proclaims liberty and restoration of possessions every fiftieth year, symbolizing God's forgiveness and renewal.
It mandates permanent transfer of property to the richest families.
It allows for indefinite slavery without hope of release.
It abolishes all property rights permanently.
questions.correctAnswer: It proclaims liberty and restoration of possessions every fiftieth year, symbolizing God's forgiveness and renewal.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:10-13 institutes the Jubilee year where liberty is proclaimed and possessions returned, typifying God's redemptive grace, forgiveness, and restoration for His people, aligning with biblical themes of salvation and renewal.

questions.question: What attribute of God is underscored by the command in Leviticus 25:17 to not oppress one another and to fear God?
options: God’s justice and holiness that demand righteous social conduct.
God’s indifference to human relationships.
God’s wrath as the sole motivation for obedience.
God’s silence concerning social ethics.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and holiness that demand righteous social conduct.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:17 connects ethical behavior with the fear of God, highlighting His justice and holiness as foundational for social righteousness and prohibiting oppression among neighbors.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Leviticus 25:20-22 and 25:1-7 communicate about God's provision during the sabbath year?
options: God promises to bless the sixth year to provide enough for the seventh year's rest, demonstrating His faithful provision and covenant care.
God expects the people to starve during the sabbath year as punishment.
God requires the people to sow and reap during the sabbath year despite the command.
God relinquishes responsibility for the people's sustenance during the sabbath year.
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to bless the sixth year to provide enough for the seventh year's rest, demonstrating His faithful provision and covenant care.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:20-22 assures that God will bless the sixth year so the people have food during the seventh year of rest commanded in 25:1-7, revealing God's providential faithfulness and care in covenant relationship.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 25:35-37, what doctrine about neighborly love and economic ethics is taught?
options: Believers must relieve the poor without charging interest, reflecting God's mercy and justice.
It permits charging high interest to the poor as a test of faith.
Neighbors should ignore the poor and focus on their own wealth.
Economic gain is the highest priority, even over mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must relieve the poor without charging interest, reflecting God's mercy and justice.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:35-37 commands mercy and forbids usury toward poor brethren, teaching God's justice and mercy in economic relations and neighborly love.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 25:39-43 teach about the dignity of the Israelite poor who become servants?
options: They are to be treated as hired servants, not bondservants, and must be freed at the Jubilee, underscoring human dignity and God's redemption.
They must be enslaved permanently without hope of freedom.
They lose all family rights and heritage permanently.
They should be punished harshly for their poverty.
questions.correctAnswer: They are to be treated as hired servants, not bondservants, and must be freed at the Jubilee, underscoring human dignity and God's redemption.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:39-43 mandates fair treatment and eventual release of poor Israelites serving as hired servants, reflecting God's concern for human dignity and foreshadowing spiritual redemption.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Leviticus 25:38 where God identifies Himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt and gave them the land?
options: God’s covenant faithfulness and sovereign deliverance.
God’s impartiality to Israel’s needs.
God’s indifference to human history.
God’s wrath without mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant faithfulness and sovereign deliverance.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:38 reveals God's covenant faithfulness and sovereign power in delivering Israel from Egypt and granting them the land, affirming His saving and sustaining attributes.

questions.question: What is the theological implication of the redemption laws in Leviticus 25:25-28 concerning property sold due to poverty?
options: God provides a means of restoration and hope through redemption, emphasizing His justice and mercy.
Property lost to poverty is permanently forfeited without hope.
The poor must remain destitute forever as punishment.
Redemption is only allowed for the wealthy.
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a means of restoration and hope through redemption, emphasizing His justice and mercy.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:25-28 teaches that relatives or even the previous owner may redeem sold property, showing God's justice and mercy by providing restoration and hope for the poor.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 25:47-54 articulate the tension between foreign sojourners' wealth and poor Israelites' servitude, and what theological principle does it reveal?
options: It teaches redemption and release for poor Israelites sold to foreigners, affirming God's justice and provision within covenant community.
It condones permanent enslavement of Israelites to foreigners.
It ignores foreign ownership and focuses only on Israelite wealth.
It forbids any economic interaction with foreigners.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches redemption and release for poor Israelites sold to foreigners, affirming God's justice and provision within covenant community.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:47-54 provides for redemption of Israelites sold to foreigners and release at Jubilee, highlighting God's justice and care for His covenant people amid social inequalities.

questions.question: What synthesis of God's holiness and social justice is evident when combining Leviticus 25:17 and Leviticus 25:43?
options: God’s holiness demands that His people fear Him and treat one another without oppression or harshness, reflecting divine justice in social ethics.
God’s holiness is unrelated to social behavior and focuses only on ritual.
Social justice is optional for those who fear God.
Oppression is allowed under the guise of religious duty.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands that His people fear Him and treat one another without oppression or harshness, reflecting divine justice in social ethics.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:17 and 25:43 together teach that fearing God includes refraining from oppression and harsh rule, showing that holiness encompasses social justice and ethical treatment of others.

questions.question: What does the command in Leviticus 25:44-46 regarding bondmen and bondmaids from heathen nations teach about Israel’s distinct covenant identity?
options: Israel is called to maintain separation in certain social aspects, preserving covenant identity distinct from surrounding nations.
Israel must assimilate fully with heathen nations socially and economically.
Israel is permitted to oppress fellow Israelites harshly.
Israel has no social distinctions in covenant obligations.
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is called to maintain separation in certain social aspects, preserving covenant identity distinct from surrounding nations.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:44-46 distinguishes between Israelites and heathen bondservants, emphasizing covenant identity and separation while prohibiting harsh rule over fellow Israelites, reflecting God's covenant holiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the Jubilee laws are impractical and promote economic chaos. What does Leviticus 25:8-12 actually teach about the purpose and timing of the Jubilee?
options: The Jubilee is a divinely ordained cyclical event every fifty years designed to restore social and economic balance, demonstrating God's justice and mercy.
The Jubilee demands constant land redistribution every year, causing instability.
The Jubilee is a myth with no practical application.
The Jubilee requires total abandonment of agriculture indefinitely.
questions.correctAnswer: The Jubilee is a divinely ordained cyclical event every fifty years designed to restore social and economic balance, demonstrating God's justice and mercy.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:8-12 prescribes a specific timing for the Jubilee every fiftieth year with the purpose of proclaiming liberty and restoring possessions, showing God’s orderly and merciful governance over society.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 25:18-19 connect obedience to God's statutes with blessings in the land, contributing to biblical theology of covenantal blessings?
options: Obedience to God's laws ensures safety and fruitful harvest, reinforcing the covenantal principle of blessing for faithfulness.
Obedience has no effect on material blessings.
God blesses disobedience to teach independence.
Covenantal blessings are random and unrelated to obedience.
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's laws ensures safety and fruitful harvest, reinforcing the covenantal principle of blessing for faithfulness.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25:18-19 links keeping God’s statutes with dwelling safely and eating abundantly, reflecting the covenant theology where obedience results in divine blessing.
